takeaway: Dobutamine is predominantly a beta 1 agonist, used in cardiogenic shock. Nitrates are venodilators, not inotropes.

question.text: Which of the following statements concerning inotropes is correct?

answer.text: Dobutamine is predominantly a β₁ receptor agonist.

lines.text: Inotropes strengthen the force of the heart's contraction.
Dobutamine is predominantly a beta 1 receptor agonist.
It is used mainly in cardiogenic shock, to make a failing heart pump harder.
Adrenaline is different. It acts on alpha, beta 1 and beta 2 receptors, with strong vasoconstriction.
Isoprenaline acts on both beta 1 and beta 2 receptors.
Nitrates are not inotropes at all.
They do not change contractility; they dilate veins and lower peripheral resistance.
lines.say: They do not change contractility; (laugh) they dilate veins and lower peripheral resistance.

lines.text: So the correct statement: dobutamine is mainly a beta 1 agonist.
